title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (October 2026)
source: EST: eia.gov/outlooks/steo/release_schedule.php lists "10/06/2026" for the October 2026 edition and states the STEO "is normally released between 12:00 pm (noon) and 12:15 pm EDT (summer)/EST (winter)" — re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200) by this event's own initial research. The date is now doubly derived: the same page's stated rule — release "on the first Tuesday following the first Thursday of each month", plus a footnote that a Federal holiday on the Monday before pushes the release to Wednesday — reproduces 10/06 exactly (2026-10-01 is a Thursday; the following Tuesday is 10-06; 10-05 is not a Federal holiday, Columbus Day 2026 being 10-12). That footnote also RESOLVES the one-day table-vs-rule mismatch eia-steo-2026-09-09 flagged as live date risk: September's normal Tuesday was 09-08, whose preceding Monday 09-07 is Labor Day, so the rule itself yields Wednesday 09-09. Primary-sourced, but this calendar defines no `confirmed` prefix for the EIA (the standing fourth schema gap the eia-steo-2026-09-09 entry named), so it stays estimate on prefix grounds, not date doubt; this lane also never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: Canonical entry written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-08), promoting the single prior proposal eia-steo-2026-10-06.from-retail-sales-2026-10-15.json, whose finding is carried forward intact: this is the last EIA publication before retail-sales-2026-10-15 (9 days prior) and the instrument that adjudicates that print's gasoline leg, because it publishes EIA's own September retail-gasoline monthly average rather than tracking pump prices. Two things this edition adjudicates that the September sibling only set up. (1) The ERCOT load line: the August STEO cut Texas 2027 electricity-load growth from 14% to 6% in one month after Governor Abbott's 2026-08-03 data-center interconnection pause, and eia-steo-2026-09-09's kill switch #4 names THIS edition (or 12/08) as the scoreboard for whether national 2027 consumption falls below 4,391 bkWh — the demand-side leg of docs/research/ai-energy-constraint.md. (2) The oil chapter's lag: August forecast Brent $87 (2026), $78/b (4Q26), $69 (2027) against a BZ=F close of 97.23 on 2026-09-08, ~24.7% above EIA's own 4Q26 number and wider than the ~22% gap measured a week earlier. Filed `low` on the sibling's own reasoning: a forecast publication sets no policy and moves no equity tape. MEASURED this session and new to this repo — the STEO-day effect does NOT reach our tracked names: across the eight 2026 editions, full-day median |move| is 0.61% for NVDA (vs 1.64% all days), 1.12% AVGO (1.61%), 1.80% MRVL (2.29%), 3.39% CRWV (3.86%), 0.89% MSFT (0.84%), and every 12:00-13:00 ET release hour sits inside the name's own p90. The 10-06 tape belongs to Marvell's morning investor day (confirmed, MRVL-keyed) and the 1:00 pm ET 3Y auction, not to this publication. Publication risk from the 2026-09-30 funding cliff is dead: H.R. 6500 (PL 119-103, signed 2026-09-02) funds agencies through 2026-12-11, and EIA published the October 2025 STEO on schedule seven days into the October 2025 lapse.
